routes.rationale: Read-only first-response-time (FRT) metric for the published 2-business-day support SLA - the route that makes that public promise falsifiable. Lives under /api/internal/admin/support/ because that IS the support operator console (ticket list, thread view, status PATCH and operator reply POST are all in the sibling route.ts), so it follows this directory's convention: authorizeRequest(request, 'support.view_tickets'), the READ code already granted to the support role by 20260612123200 - not support.manage_tickets, and no new permission code was invented (P9). Both query params are clamped server-side (days 1..365 default 30, queue_limit 1..500 default 100); there is no id or tenant parameter, so nothing caller-supplied steers a row filter. The summary is windowed by ticket created_at, but the work queue is deliberately NOT windowed - a six-month-old ignored ticket is the single most important row an operator can see.
routes.serviceRoleUse: Service-role is required, not convenience: NEITHER table read here has any operator/admin/support-role SELECT policy. support_tickets has exactly two SELECT policies, both requester-anchored ('Users can read own tickets' on own auth email or own student_id; support_tickets_self_select on own student_id). support_ticket_replies (20260814000012) has exactly three (_owner_select, _owner_insert, _service_role_all), and that migration states the design outright: the operator surface goes through the service-role client, with authorization enforced in the route by authorizeRequest(), not by RLS. An RLS-scoped client would therefore show an operator only the tickets that operator personally filed, and this metric would report breach_count 0 / meeting_promise true over a near-empty set - silently certifying that we meet the SLA precisely because it cannot see the breaches. A metric that fails toward 'all clear' is worse than no metric, so RLS here is a silent-zero rather than a second line of defense. The sibling /api/internal/admin/support is already ledgered, reads the same two tables and carries the same permission gate. Bounded surface: read-only, no writes or RPCs; three capped SELECTs (tickets in window LIMIT 5000; still-open tickets LIMIT 2000; replies chunked by ticket_id IN <=200, filtered is_internal=false AND author_role IN operator/admin/system). P13 field whitelist: support_tickets carries email, user_name, subject, message, device_info and admin_notes and NONE is selected - the ticket projection is pinned to the single TICKET_COLUMNS constant 'id, category, status, created_at, resolved_at' and the reply projection to 'ticket_id, created_at, author_role', so no message body and no author identity can reach the response. Output is aggregates plus a (ticket_id, category, status, created_at, age) queue: UUIDs only. DB errors return a generic body so the PostgREST string cannot echo the ticket-id list back; nothing is logged or audited (read-only aggregate). Ledgered in scripts/admin-client-allowlist.json. Ratchet-down path: add a SECURITY DEFINER RPC get_support_first_response_metrics(p_days, p_queue_limit) that gates on the existing baseline helper check_permission(auth.uid(), 'support.view_tickets') and projects the same eight columns, GRANT EXECUTE to authenticated, then move this route to the RLS-scoped client and prune both justifications. Note the support_ticket_first_response view proposed in this route's header comment is NOT that path - it is security_invoker and granted to service_role only, so it still needs this client. Do not instead add an operator SELECT policy on support_tickets: that widens RLS over the full PII row and trades a narrow column whitelist for table-level exposure.

Student-owned READ of the caller's OWN daily quota (P0-1 display/enforcement gap). Gated by authorizeRequest() with the student-role permission for the requested feature — 'foxy.chat' for foxy_chat, 'quiz.attempt' for quiz (both granted to the student role by migration 20260612123200). The student id is resolved ONLY from the session (auth.studentId, derived from students.auth_user_id = caller); no studentId is accepted from the query string or body, so there is no cross-student read path. EVERY unrecognised ?feature= value — inherited Object.prototype keys included — is rejected 400 before authorizeRequest and before any DB call, with NO exception. Architect-verified against shipped source 2026-07-29: the FEATURE_PERMISSION lookup is a new Map<string, string> (route.ts:82-85) whose get() consults no prototype chain, and the guard is typeof permission !== 'string' (route.ts:95-100), so inherited keys are unreachable by construction and only one of the two allowlisted feature values can ever reach get_plan_limit. HISTORY (CLOSED, kept so the fix is not re-litigated): the pre-ship draft used a plain object literal typed Record<string, string> (which, with noUncheckedIndexedAccess off, typed the index as a non-optional string and gave the compiler no signal), so inherited keys returned truthy and slipped past the !permission guard. The impact was broader than this entry first recorded: a STUDENT caller got an unhandled 500 (rbac.ts:785 calls .split() on the non-string permission in the deny branch, which sits above the try), while a super_admin caller took the isSuperAdmin short-circuit at rbac.ts:779-780 that skips the permission check entirely, so a prototype key DID reach get_plan_limit and land in its generous ai_calls_total ELSE arm. That path also required the caller to own a student row, and get_plan_limit is read-only, so the over-generous number was display-only and never raised the ENFORCED cap in check_and_record_usage. Both paths are closed, pinned by 4 tests covering 8 prototype keys. Response is four integers plus a boolean — no names, emails, phones, school identity, or roster data (P13).
routes.serviceRoleUse: Architect-reviewed 2026-07-29. Required, not convenience: migration 20260729130400 §5 (re-asserting 20260516040000/20260516050000) REVOKEs EXECUTE ON public.get_plan_limit(uuid, text) FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated, so an RLS-scoped browser session literally cannot call the enforcement authority. Reading the SAME function that check_and_record_usage() enforces from is the whole point of the route — a second, client-side derivation is exactly the drift this closes. Scope is minimal: one STABLE read-only RPC plus one own-row SELECT on student_daily_usage, both keyed on the session-derived studentId. The route never inserts, updates, increments or grants; the hard gate remains checkAndIncrementQuota -> check_and_record_usage in /api/foxy. Input reaching the service-role client is CLOSED, not merely narrow — re-verified against shipped source 2026-07-29 now that the earlier prototype-chain hole is fixed: the only caller-controlled value forwarded to get_plan_limit is p_feature, and it can only be one of the two keys of the FEATURE_PERMISSION Map ('foxy_chat' or 'quiz'), because a Map lookup plus a typeof permission !== 'string' guard returns 400 before the client is touched for every other input, inherited Object.prototype keys included. p_student_id is session-derived and never request-supplied. RATCHET-DOWN PATH (follow-up, not blocking): add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER wrapper get_my_plan_limit(p_feature text) GRANTed to authenticated, then move this route to the RLS-scoped client and prune this entry. Do NOT simply GRANT EXECUTE on get_plan_limit(uuid, text) to authenticated — it takes p_student_id as an argument and performs no auth.uid() check, so that would let any authenticated user read any student's plan cap.

routes.rationale: Foxy North-Star Phase 5 lane U10: caller's OWN leaderboard band (percentile + rank + neighbours) for the requested period. authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view'); studentId resolved from auth.uid() only — ?student_id ignored.
routes.serviceRoleUse: Service-role read of the get_leaderboard_percentile RPC scoped to the session-derived studentId (never a request-supplied id); RPC returns caller-owned band + PII-free neighbour names only. Ratchet-down path: replace with an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER RPC then move to the RLS-scoped client.

routes.rationale: Leaderboard SEV1 Pattern-B repair: the caller's OWN class leaderboard, with class membership resolved server-side from class_students (students.class_id does not exist). authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view') - a permission held by student, teacher and tutor, hence 'auth' rather than 'student', matching every sibling /api/v1/leaderboard/*. studentId is resolved from the session only; a ?student_id param is ignored (P13). Additionally gated by ff_class_leaderboard_v1 (404 when OFF). NO serviceRoleUse entry by design: this route uses the RLS-scoped createSupabaseRouteClient, so the class_students own-enrollment policy plus the already-SECURITY-DEFINER get_class_leaderboard RPC (EXECUTE granted to authenticated) are a real second line of defence behind authorizeRequest. It is correspondingly absent from scripts/admin-client-allowlist.json.

Leaderboard SEV1 Pattern-B repair: daily-challenge streak board (peer rows plus the caller's own row). authorizeRequest('leaderboard.view') - a permission held by student, teacher and tutor, hence 'auth' rather than 'student', matching every sibling /api/v1/leaderboard/*. The caller's own students.id comes from the session only; a ?student_id param is ignored (P13). Response is Cache-Control: private because it carries a caller-specific 'me' block.
routes.serviceRoleUse: Service-role is required, not convenience: challenge_streaks RLS is own-row-only (challenge_streaks_student_select) and students_select_merged is own/teacher-of/guardian-of, so a cross-student board is structurally impossible under RLS - the page previously read it from the BROWSER and rendered the single returned row as a 'Top Streaks' board. Bounded surface: two capped read-only SELECTs (challenge_streaks at or above the visibility threshold, then students by id IN the surviving set), projected through an explicit P13 whitelist - peers get rank/student_id/name/grade/current_streak plus only those badges already implied by the exposed current_streak; best_streak, avatar_url, school, city, last_challenge_date and the mercy-day counters never leave the server. No request-supplied id reaches any filter. Ledgered in scripts/admin-client-allowlist.json. Ratchet-down path: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER get_streak_leaderboard(p_limit) GRANTed to authenticated, mirroring get_class_leaderboard, then move to the RLS-scoped client and prune both this justification and the allowlist entry.

routes.rationale: Leaderboard SEV1 Pattern-B repair: the CALLER'S OWN earned titles - own-data only, no peer titles ever. authorizeRequest('progress.view_own'); studentId is resolved from the session only and a ?student_id param is ignored (P13). Declared 'auth' to stay consistent with the path-prefix taxonomy the manifest generator derives ('student' is reserved for /api/student|students|v2/student prefixes) and with every sibling /api/v1/leaderboard/*; an authorized caller that has no students row receives an empty list, never another student's rows. Field whitelist: id, title, title_hi, icon, tier, source, earned_at - source_id and student_id are deliberately omitted. Cache-Control: private.
routes.serviceRoleUse: Service-role is required, not convenience: student_titles has RLS ENABLED with EXACTLY ONE policy, 'Service role full access on student_titles'. There is no student SELECT policy at all, so an RLS-scoped client reads 0 rows for every caller and the 'My Titles' tab was permanently empty. The fix is a service-role read scoped SERVER-SIDE to the caller's own students.id, NOT an RLS change (P8: no policy is weakened). Bounded surface: one read-only SELECT on student_titles filtered on the session-derived student_id and is_active, capped at 50 rows. No cross-student path exists. Ledgered in scripts/admin-client-allowlist.json. Ratchet-down path: add an auth.uid()-anchored SECURITY DEFINER get_my_titles() GRANTed to authenticated, then move to the RLS-scoped client and prune both this justification and the allowlist entry.
